clue.text: Excessively absent from Scots city

parts.note: OTT, short for over the top, means excessively
awa is the Scots form of away, meaning absent

explanation.surface: Someone notes that a person has been missing far too long from a Scottish town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scots city' reads as a Scottish place, but 'from Scots' belongs to the wordplay, flagging a Scots word, and the city is the Canadian capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Ottawa is the capital of Canada, an example of a city.

clue.text: After mistake, appeal accepted by politician in province

indicators.note: something accepted by another is taken inside it, so the politician holds the other pieces

parts.note: a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

indicators.note: the appeal comes after the mistake in the order of letters

parts.note: to err is to make a mistake
IT is crossword shorthand for sex appeal

explanation.surface: A politician takes up a plea from a region after some blunder there.
explanation.walkthrough: IT for sex appeal is an old crossword convention; 'After' puts the mistake first in the pair that the politician takes in.
explanation.definitionFit: A province is an administrative region, much as a territory is in countries such as Canada or Australia.

clue.text: Veteran once having to do with capturing islands

indicators.note: a word capturing another holds it inside, so the islands go within

parts.note: anent is an old word for concerning, so 'once' marks it as archaic
CI stands for the Channel Islands

explanation.surface: An old soldier is linked to the seizing of some islands in times past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'once' marks the wordplay word as archaic; 'Veteran' looks like a soldier but works as the adjective-turned-noun for someone very old.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancient is an old term for a very old person or a veteran soldier.

clue.text: Ruler of a southern state

parts.note: GA is the abbreviation for Georgia, a state in the American South

explanation.surface: A governor heads a state in the American South.
explanation.definitionFit: An aga is a title for a commander or chief official in Ottoman and Muslim countries, so a ruler.

clue.text: Decoration, not the first in Lent — that's to be regretted

parts.note: BEM is the British Empire Medal, an honour awarded in the UK

indicators.note: the opening letter is dropped from the word that follows

parts.note: lent, as a verb, means loaned

explanation.surface: Someone notes that a medal handed out during the Christian season of Lent is something to be sorry about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lent' is not the Christian season here but a past tense; LOANED loses its L, giving OANED. 'that's to be' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: To bemoan something is to lament it, so bemoaned means regretted.

clue.text: Black without? Isn't that sweet?

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
less means without, as in a meal less pudding

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether going without sugar in black coffee is still sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Bless!' is a fond British exclamation said on seeing something cute or touching.

clue.text: Unnaturally desiring gum, touring Black Sea resort

indicators.note: the gum goes round the resort, holding it inside as a tour circles a place

parts.note: mastic is a resin used as gum
Sochi is a Russian resort on the Black Sea

explanation.surface: Someone craves chewing gum while travelling around a Russian holiday town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unnaturally' looks like an anagram signal, but it belongs to the definition; Sochi hosted the 2014 Winter Olympics.
explanation.definitionFit: Masochistic describes taking pleasure in one's own pain, a desire long labelled perverse or unnatural.

clue.text: Lean out, about to pinch girl

indicators.note: one piece goes about the other, surrounding it
out signals that the letters of lean are put out of order

parts.note: to nab is to steal or pinch

explanation.surface: A thin person goes out to steal from a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: LEAN is rearranged as ANEL, which goes about NAB to give AN-NAB-EL; 'to' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Annabel is a female first name, so a girl's name.

clue.text: Order Chambers shortly, could one say?

indicators.note: the clue asks whether this is how the words are spoken, flagging a sound-alike

parts.note: Chambers is a well-known dictionary, shortened to 'a dict'

explanation.surface: Someone asks about calling a set of rooms, or a law office, by a short name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chambers' looks like a barrister's offices, but it is the Chambers Dictionary, cut short to 'a dict', which said aloud resembles the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An edict is an official decree, that is, an order issued by an authority.

clue.text: Consider cutting salary means ruin

indicators.note: one piece cutting another goes into it, splitting it

parts.note: a wage is pay, a salary
reck is an old verb meaning to heed or consider

explanation.surface: Someone thinks that reducing pay will bring disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: Reck survives mainly in 'reckless'; 'means' only links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Wreckage is the remains of something destroyed, so a ruin.

clue.text: Writer's name is put back, where one was out of play

definitions.text: where one was out of play

indicators.note: put back means the whole run of letters is read in reverse

parts.note: a nib is the writing tip of a pen, a writer

explanation.surface: An author's name is restored to where a player once sat out a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put back' turns the whole run, writer, name and 'is', round together; 'Writer's' gives only the pen part, the 's being no letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The sin bin is the area where a penalised player in rugby or ice hockey sits out for a time.

clue.text: Succession of bars that are conducted?

definitions.text: Succession of bars that are conducted?

parts.words: Succession of bars that are conducted?
parts.note: bars of music that are carried along, as through tubes, rather than led by a conductor

explanation.surface: A run of musical bars led by a conductor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conducted' suggests a conductor with a baton, but here it means channelled, as water or sound through pipes.
explanation.definitionFit: Recorded background music relayed through speakers in shops is music carried along to the listener.

clue.text: Moliere character worked in metaphors

indicators.note: worked means the letters are worked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A French playwright's figure is drawn using figures of speech.
explanation.walkthrough: IN and METAPHORS are shuffled together into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Le Misanthrope is a comedy by Moliere whose title character Alceste is a misanthrope.

clue.text: Only last of claret in cask

parts.note: but means only, as in 'but a child'

indicators.note: the final letter of the next word is taken

explanation.surface: Just the final drop of red wine remains in the barrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A butt is a large barrel for wine or beer, a kind of cask.

clue.text: Major river leads right to this?

definitions.text: Major river leads right to this?

parts.note: the Po is Italy's longest river

indicators.note: leads means the opening letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A great river flows straight down to a harbour town.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes a harbour at the river's mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: A port is a harbour town, which a major river may carry ships to.

clue.text: With energy, strike piano — this'll lighten things up

parts.note: spirit means energy or vigour, as in playing with spirit
to lam is to beat or strike
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: Someone bangs at a piano keyboard with gusto.
explanation.definitionFit: A spirit lamp burns methylated spirit to give light.

clue.text: Princess gained heart of king with magic touch

indicators.note: heart means only the inner letters are kept, the first and last going

parts.note: Midas, the mythical king whose touch turned everything to gold

explanation.surface: A princess came to love a king with a golden touch.
explanation.walkthrough: MIDAS loses its first and last letters to leave the middle; 'gained' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Princess Ida is the heroine of the Gilbert and Sullivan opera named after her, from Tennyson's poem The Princess.

clue.text: Attraction of Emma — thing's not hard to work out

indicators.note: to work out signals that the letters are worked into another order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: H is the pencil abbreviation for hard, and it is removed

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: What a woman finds appealing in Emma is not too difficult to discover.
explanation.walkthrough: THINGS loses H to give TINGS, which is shuffled with EMMA.
explanation.definitionFit: Magnetism is a power of attraction, physical or personal.

clue.text: Demonstration of mutual regard

parts.note: regard read as gaze: two people looking at each other at once

explanation.surface: A show of respect between two people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regard' reads as esteem, but here it is the literal act of looking.
explanation.definitionFit: Two people meeting each other's gaze directly is a literal case of looking at one another.

clue.text: Study works, and what they relate to

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
a text is a written work

explanation.surface: A student reads literary works and the background to them.
explanation.definitionFit: A context is the setting a passage or event belongs to and is understood through.

clue.text: Decision in favour of visiting republic

definitions.meaning: the resolve to make a trip, as in a choice about whether or not to travel
a West African country with a president

explanation.surface: A choice is made for a trip to a country.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase 'to go' expresses a decision to travel, and Togo is a republic in West Africa.

clue.text: Rock it, said composer

indicators.note: said signals a sound-alike of the words before

parts.note: to rock something is to tip it

explanation.surface: Someone tells a musician to play loud rock music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock' suggests the music, but it means tilt.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Michael Tippett was an English twentieth-century composer.

clue.text: River enters dark-coloured lake

indicators.note: the river enters, so goes inside the other piece

parts.note: tan is a brown, darkish colour

explanation.surface: A stream flows into a murky pool.
explanation.definitionFit: A tarn is a small mountain lake, especially in northern England.

clue.text: Free spirit — one connected with TV, say

indicators.note: say signals that the words are spoken to give the answer's sound

parts.note: an aerial is the antenna connected to a television set

explanation.surface: An independent soul is one hooked up to television.
explanation.walkthrough: In Shakespeare's The Tempest the spirit Ariel is set free by Prospero.
explanation.definitionFit: Ariel is the airy spirit in The Tempest who longs for, and wins, freedom.

clue.text: The police struggle to run surveillance equipment

indicators.note: struggle signals the letters writhing into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Officers find it hard to operate their monitoring gear.
explanation.walkthrough: THE POLICE is rearranged and R added at the end; 'to' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: A helicopter is used by police forces to watch from the air, a piece of surveillance kit.

clue.text: Cause excitement, keeping right round mark on road

indicators.note: one piece goes round the other, enclosing it

parts.note: a lien is a legal right to keep property until a debt is paid
V-shaped chevron marks are painted on British motorways to space cars

explanation.surface: Someone stirs things up while driving round a road marking on the right side.
explanation.walkthrough: The legal right called a lien is a right to keep, hence 'keeping right'; 'round' holds the road mark inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To liven is to make lively, stirring up excitement.

clue.text: Old politician takes care of installing freezer

indicators.note: the outer piece is installing, putting inside itself, the other

parts.note: an icer is something that ices or freezes

explanation.surface: An elderly statesman arranges for a fridge to be fitted.
explanation.walkthrough: ICER goes between C and O; 'takes' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Cicero was a statesman and orator of ancient Rome.

clue.text: By sea, I took a moderate course

parts.note: via means by way of
the Med is the Mediterranean Sea

explanation.surface: Someone recounts taking a middle way by sailing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'took' only links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Via media is Latin for the middle way, a compromise between extremes.

clue.text: Unable to start to confront expert

indicators.note: unable to start means losing the first letter

parts.note: to face is to confront

explanation.surface: Someone cannot bring themselves to take on a master.
explanation.definitionFit: An ace is a highly skilled person, an expert.

clue.text: Cow last to be canned?

indicators.note: read with canned, the phrase means to be put inside a tin, so one piece goes within

parts.note: Sn is the chemical symbol for tin, the metal of a can
latter means the last of two

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether the final cow should be put in a tin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cow' is a slur for a woman; 'canned' becomes the chemical symbol for tin, which wraps the word for last.
explanation.definitionFit: Slattern and cow are both old derogatory terms for an untidy or unpleasant woman.

clue.text: Medical area's nothing to doctor: so shut up patients?

parts.note: ENT stands for ear, nose and throat, a medical speciality
O looks like zero, nothing
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree

explanation.surface: A clinic says its department has no doctor, so patients are told to be quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shut up' means silence, but here it is to enclose: what one does to patients who have died.
explanation.definitionFit: To entomb is to shut up in a tomb, the fate of patients whose treatment failed.
